sources.name: Tuneskipet
sources.finding: Named archaeological-site and visitor-attraction point at the surviving memorial and marked ship-grave location on Haugen farm.

sources.name: Tuneskipet
sources.finding: The ship was excavated from Båthaugen at Haugen farm on Rolvsøy in 1867. The mound was one of Norway's largest and had been heavily reduced before excavation.

sources.name: Historien om Fredrikstad
sources.finding: The municipality identifies the Tune ship as a Rolvsøy find and distinguishes the local find history from the museum object in Oslo.

sources.name: The Tune Viking Ship Reconsidered
sources.finding: The archaeological study identifies Nedre Haugen on Rolvsøy as the find farm and documents Båthaugen as the ship-burial context.

sources.name: Tidlige tider på Rolvsøy
sources.finding: The local history source describes the present memorial at Haugen and confirms that the original mound was not reconstructed.

rejectedCandidates.reason: The canonical record is the Østfold findspot, not the preserved ship as a museum object.
The farm confirms identity but is less precise than the named archaeological findspot.
The point lies approximately 1.26 km southwest of the identified findspot and has no source contract.

representationLimits: The point represents the marked Båthaugen findspot and memorial area.
The 260 m gameplay radius is not the original mound geometry, legal protection boundary or full Haugen farm archaeological landscape.
The ship itself is preserved at the Viking Age Museum in Oslo and is not physically present at the findspot.
